description: The Apollo 11 lunar module (Eagle) on a variable-mass 3D bond graph: powered descent from PDI to touchdown on the landing gear, the landing phase flown from the dashboard, and the ascent to orbit. Checks against an independent scipy integration of the same equations (tight), analytic rocket-equation cases (exact), and the Apollo 11 Mission Report, Apollo by the Numbers, TN D-6846/D-6850 and the ALSJ transcript (honest tolerances; each note says whether the quantity was fitted).

PUBLISHED (flight, indicative): no primary-strut stroking was recorded on Apollo 11 (TN D-6850 table V), so no strut reached its 4,500 lb honeycomb cartridge, let alone the 9,500 lb one behind it (TN D-6850 fig. 6). The model's struts are rigid and a pad's force is shared in reality by the primary and two secondary struts, so the check is against the 9,500 lb level; the model's peak (forward pad, as the LM rocks onto it from a 4.5 deg tilt) is about 10 % above 4,500 lb

TSIOLKOVSKY (analytic): no gravity, thrust held vertical, so the speed is c ln(m0/m) = 3034.18 m/s * ln(4888.2/3364.68); the engine burns at full thrust from t = 0, m(t) = m0 - T t / c. Tests the variable-mass bond graph (MI + outflow MR).

ROCKET EQUATION (analytic): in a hover T = m g, so m(t) = m0 exp(-g t / c) and the usable propellant (300 kg) is gone at t = (c/g) ln(m0/m_empty) = 76.556 s
free fall after the engine quits: the lagged thrust T0 exp(-t/tau) with T0 = m g still gives g tau of velocity, so 3 s later rdot = -g (3 s - tau) (analytic)
